key_insight: A purely physics-driven P-PINN can learn continuous parametric periodic-flow solutions and use them to predict finite-amplitude aeroelastic responses without long transient CFD runs.
engineering_relevance: This enables fast, reusable aeroelastic analysis across operating and structural parameters, reducing the cost of repeated high-fidelity fluid-structure simulations.
method: Impose temporal periodicity over one motion cycle with a Periodic Physics-Informed Neural Network (P-PINN).
Treat flow conditions and motion parameters as network inputs to build a continuous parametric model of periodic flow fields and aerodynamic loads.
Couple the learned aerodynamic model to a single-degree-of-freedom structural equation via first-order harmonic balance to compute response amplitude and frequency.
evidence_signal: The framework is validated on forced-motion circular-cylinder and airfoil cases, reproducing periodic forces, surface loads, and instantaneous flow fields, and also matches fully coupled CFD/CSD aeroelastic results for an elastically mounted cylinder.
watch_item: Performance depends on accurate training over the relevant parameter range, so extrapolation beyond sampled flow or motion conditions may be unreliable.
paper_title: A Physics-Driven Framework for Parametric Periodic-Flow Modeling and Finite-Amplitude Aeroelastic Response Analysis
